Broken detection genuinely only fires for test-shaped ids; medium because the only consumer is a devtools issues panel, not a data gate.

The pattern at line 3 is anchored only by \b (no ^...$), so test() is a substring match, and lines 53-59 push missingId: value (the whole string); the filter in referenceIndex.ts:65 then checks existingIds.has on that whole string. Code-accurate, but only manifests for free-text containing an entity_ token, which does not occur in real data, so impact is narrow.

existingIds.has(value) at line 41 is a case-sensitive JS Set lookup while ENTITY_ID_PATTERN carries the i flag, so a case-variant reference (entity_A vs key entity_a) misses the Set, matches the pattern, and is reported broken. The sequence holds against the code, but only affects entity_-prefixed ids that exist solely in tests, so it is real but very narrow.

Because line 52 gates broken.push on the entity_ pattern, a reference to a real but missing nanoid/slug id yields an empty broken list; the sole consumer useIssuesPanel.ts:33 surfaces refs.broken as the module's dangling-reference report, so it shows a permanent false all-clear on production data. Severity medium not high: this feeds an author-facing devtools diagnostic, not a save/runtime path, so no data loss or crash results.

Technically true but cannot affect current behavior, hence trivial; it is latent-only redundancy, not a live defect.

Line 61 is a bare return reached when a non-existing string value fails the entity_ pattern, so a dangling reference to a real missing id (e.g. a payload blueprintId or pool optionId) produces no incoming and no broken entry and is dropped untraced. Real silent-failure; impact is confined to the completeness of the devtools issues panel rather than runtime state, so medium.
